newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs to export 5.6 mln T grain from '96 harvest.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs to export 5.6 mln T grain from '96 harvest.

text.p: Kazakhstan will export 5.6 million tonnes of grain from this year's net harvest of 11.6 million tonnes, Deputy Prime Minister Zhanybek Karibzhanov said on Monday.
"We (Kazakhstan) plan to export around 5.6 million tonnes of grain this year -- that's 55 percent up on last year," he told a news conference in the capital Almaty.
Karibzhanov said buyers included neighbouring Russia and the Central Asian states of Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan and Tajikistan.
He said Turkey and China had also shown interest and that some grains had been exported to western Europe earlier this year.
Speaking of grain quality, he said: "Compared to last year, the quality is much better; it is up to world standards."
Some agricultural specialists have said Kazakhstan needs a net harvest of at least 13 million tonnes in order to export at least five million tonnes.
Karibzhanov said state purchases of grain for strategic reserves would not rise above last year's level of around one million tonnes.
